editorial_notes: Written about the PREVIOUS edition, from published reporting on it, to help a reader decide on the next one. No rating: the sources are news reports and organiser statements, which describe how an event was run, not how runners rated it. A score needs participant evidence -- race reports, runner blogs, attributed quotes -- and without it would be invention.
title: Arutmin Borneo Run 2026 Review: What the 2025 Edition Was Like
seo_title: Arutmin Borneo Run 2026 Review | Banjarbaru, South Kalimantan
meta_description: Arutmin Borneo Run review: the 2025 edition drew 4,050 runners and sold out in five minutes. What that means for entering the 2026 race in Banjarbaru.
dek: South Kalimantan's biggest road race sold every one of its 4,050 places in five minutes last year. Here is what the 2025 edition was like, and what it tells you about getting into the 2026 race on 1 November.
verdict: The Arutmin Borneo Run is the race that defines road running in South Kalimantan, and the 2025 edition showed why: 4,050 runners on Sunday 23 November, up from around 3,000 the year before [1][2], with every place gone within five minutes of registration opening [2]. It is run on a PASI-certified route from the governor's office area in Banjarbaru [1][2], and it is unusually deliberate about inclusion -- student slots, a training plan for beginners, and a welcome for disabled and older runners [2]. The single most important thing to know about the 2026 race is that you will need to be ready the moment entries open.

sections.heading: The 2025 Edition in Numbers
paragraphs: The 2025 race was held on Sunday 23 November, starting and finishing in the area around the governor's office in Banjarbaru [1]. It drew 4,050 runners across three distances: 1,200 in the half marathon, 2,000 in the 10 km and about 850 in the 5 km, a figure that included 110 students from South Kalimantan [1].

That was a sharp rise from around 3,000 runners the previous year [2], and the event reported it was in its seventeenth year [2]. For a province with very little on the national running calendar, a field of that size makes this the reference race for the region rather than one option among several.

sections.heading: Five Minutes to Sell Out
paragraphs: The detail that should shape your plans is how fast the 2025 edition filled. According to the organisers' own reporting, every place was taken within five minutes of registration opening [2]. That is a waiting-room-and-refresh situation, not a sign-up-when-you-get-round-to-it one.
If you intend to run the 2026 edition, find out when registration opens and treat that moment as the real start of the race. Missing it probably means missing the event.

sections.heading: How It Is Run
paragraphs: The race has been managed by IdeaRun since 2023 [2]. The 2025 route was certified by PASI, Indonesia's athletics federation, and the organisers describe professional safety arrangements including hydration points, an emergency plan and medical coordination [2].

2025 was also the first time a gun start was used across every category in South Kalimantan [1][2] -- a small thing, but a sign of an event trying to run to national standard rather than as a community fun run.

Inclusion is a stated priority rather than an afterthought. The organisers reserve slots for student runners in the 5 km, offer a twelve-week training programme for beginners, and welcome disabled and older runners both as participants and as members of the team [2]. Finishers in 2025 were also handed a local street snack, with 12,000 portions of pentol distributed to support local traders [2].

sections.heading: What to Expect in 2026
paragraphs: The 2026 edition is scheduled for Sunday 1 November, again over 5 km, 10 km and the half marathon [3]. That is three weeks earlier in the year than 2025, so do not assume last year's timing when you plan.
Nothing published so far suggests the format is changing. Expect the same three distances, the same organiser and, if demand holds, the same five-minute scramble for places.

sections.heading: Should You Enter?
paragraphs: If you run in Kalimantan, yes. It is the largest and best-organised road race in the province, the course is federation-certified, and the half marathon field of more than a thousand is big enough to find people running your pace.
If you are travelling in for it, the harder question is logistics rather than quality: you need a place first, and on 2025's evidence that is the part most likely to go wrong.
This review is compiled from published reporting on the previous edition and the organisers' own announcements. It is not a first-hand race report, and nobody from this site ran the race.

faqs.question: How many people ran the Arutmin Borneo Run in 2025?
faqs.answer: 4,050 runners took part on Sunday 23 November 2025: 1,200 in the half marathon, 2,000 in the 10 km and about 850 in the 5 km, including 110 students. That was up from around 3,000 runners the previous year, making it South Kalimantan's largest road race.

faqs.question: How quickly does the Arutmin Borneo Run sell out?
faqs.answer: Very quickly. The organisers reported that every place for the 2025 edition was taken within five minutes of registration opening. Anyone planning to run should find out when entries open and be ready at that exact moment.

faqs.question: Is the Arutmin Borneo Run course certified?
faqs.answer: Yes. The 2025 route was certified by PASI, Indonesia's national athletics federation. The race also used a gun start across every category for the first time in South Kalimantan, and is managed by IdeaRun.
